newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes higher despite steadier dollar.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes higher despite steadier dollar.

text.p: The price of gold eased on Tuesday after Monday had seen it hit resistance in a rally to around $350 an ounce, highest for a month.

But it steadied later, and precious metals prices generally were just above morning levels at the London Tuesday afternoon fixing. This was after New York opened slightly firmer and despite a more stable dollar.

The precious metals also held their ground against an announcement from Moscow that a five-month delay to Russian platinum and palladium exports could be over soon. Palladium has been at two-year highs on the lack of Russian shipments.
A rally in gold from around $340-343 last week, helped by a weaker dollar, lost confidence late Monday at around $350.00 where heavy selling was encountered.

But gold fixed in London on Tuesday afternoon at $348.90 per ounce against $347.30 previously and $348.20 on Monday afternoon. The June contract on New York Comex futures was at $350.10, up $1.40, at the fix.
"There are a lot of positions and profit taking around. People are trying to keep their book reasonably square because they are very unsure about the market," one dealer said.
The dollar, firming to over 119 yen but held at under 1.70 marks, should have put pressure on precious metals prices but did not do so.
"The metal prices have been moving inversely to the currencies which is what they are supposed to do. But not today," a dealer said.
Although the technical background to the gold market remained positive after its rally last week and on Monday, dealers forecast a regrouping ahead of any further advances.

"The feeling is that we may try and find support. The 100-day moving average is $351. That's going to be a major resistance level," said one. But he added that if platinum and palladium advanced again, gold and silver would also benefit.
Technical analyst Karen Jones of Credit Suisse First Boston said gold could drop to $345 or even $343.50 without losing its sparkle on the charts. But she saw resistance at $354-$355.

Platinum and palladium lost ground initially when Russian officials confirmed export talks with Japan had begun.But later they edged up. "It's a very jittery market although the only logical direction is downwards," a dealer said.
Platinum was valued at $388.75/$389.75 down $7.50 and palladium was $4.00 off at $169.509/$170.50. Silver was five cents lower at $4.85/$4.87. --Brian Spoors +44 171 542 8058
